sections.title: DAKOTAS/UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: INITIALLY...A MCS IS EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING THIS MORNING IN VICINITY OF FAR EASTERN ND/NORTHERN MN. WITH ANY EARLY DAY ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY WANE THROUGH THE MORNING...A STRONG ELEVATED MIXED LAYER /EML/ SHOULD OTHERWISE CAP THE WARM/MOIST SECTOR FOR MUCH OF THE AFTERNOON. A PROGRESSIVE UPPER TROUGH IS EXPECTED TO CROSS THE NORTHERN PORTIONS OF ALBERTA/SASKATCHEWAN/MANITOBA THROUGH TONIGHT...WHILE SEVERAL LOW AMPLITUDE DISTURBANCES OVER THE ROCKIES /ROUNDING THE UPPER SOUTHERN TIER UPPER RIDGE/ GRADUALLY COME INTO PHASE WITH THE STRONGER WESTERLIES ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF THE WESTERN CANADA SYSTEM. AS THIS OCCURS...A SURFACE LOW/ASSOCIATED SURFACE TROUGH WILL SHIFT EASTWARD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS...PRIOR TO EVENTUALLY BEING OVERTAKEN BY A SOUTHEASTWARD-MOVING COLD FRONT LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. AT THE SAME TIME...A WARM FRONT /AUGMENTED BY EARLY DAY CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW/ WILL GRADUALLY SHIFT NORTHWARD ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS/UPPER MS VALLEY...WITH A VERY MOIST /LOWER AND PERHAPS SOME MIDDLE 70S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS/ AND STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS ALONG/SOUTH OF THE WARM FRONT BY THIS AFTERNOON. AS HEIGHT FALLS/COOLING ALOFT BEGINS TO GRAZE THE DAKOTAS...INI

sections.title: NORTHEAST STATES/NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: EASTERN CANADIAN UPPER TROUGH WILL DIG SOUTHEASTWARD OVER QUEBEC/EASTERN ONTARIO TOWARD NEW ENGLAND/NORTHEAST STATES THROUGH TONIGHT...WITH ASSOCIATED COOLING/STRENGTHENING CYCLONIC FLOW ALOFT AS FAR SOUTH AS THE MID-ATLANTIC STATES. WITH RELATIVELY STEEP LAPSE RATES/SUFFICIENT CAPE BY AFTERNOON...MULTIPLE SOUTHEASTWARD-MOVING BANDS OF STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP/INCREASE THIS AFTERNOON...WITH SUCH DEVELOPMENT FOCUSED IN VICINITY OF A SURFACE TROUGH ACROSS NEW ENGLAND/NEAR THE EASTERN SEABOARD AND/OR ALONG ONE OR MORE SOUTHEASTWARD MOVING WEAK COLD FRONTS ACROSS THE NORTHEAST/NEW ENGLAND. SUSTAINED MULTICELLS ALONG WITH A FEW SUPERCELLS CAN BE EXPECTED...WITH DAMAGING WINDS/SEVERE HAIL AS THE PRIMARY HAZARDS.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST STATES/GULF COAST REGION
sections.text: ALONG/SOUTH OF A SLOW MOVING FRONT ACROSS THE REGION...POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING COMBINED WITH A HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT AIRMASS WILL YIELD ISOLATED TO SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. DOWNBURSTS CAPABLE OF LOCALIZED WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN.

sections.title: WESTERN CONUS
sections.text: BETWEEN THE SOUTH-CENTRAL CONUS CENTERED UPPER RIDGE AND MODEST CYCLONIC WEST-SOUTHWESTERLIES OVER THE WESTERN STATES...POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING COMBINED WITH A BROAD CORRIDOR OF RELATIVELY HIGH PW VALUES WILL SUPPORT SOME STRONGER STORMS CAPABLE OF ISOLATED DOWNBURSTS/PERHAPS SOME HAIL THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. ..GUYER/ROGERS.. 08/01/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BROAD ANTICYCLONE WILL REMAIN MORE OR LESS STNRY OVER THE CNTRL/SRN PLNS THROUGH TUE. TWO SIGNIFICANT SHORTWAVE TROUGHS...ONE NOW OVER AB AND THE OTHER OVER JAMES BAY...WILL IMPACT TSTM DEVELOPMENT OVER THE LWR 48. THE AB SYSTEM WILL PROGRESS E INTO ERN MB BY THE END OF THE PERIOD AS A WEAKER IMPULSE FARTHER S...IN THE STREAM OF FLOW IMMEDIATELY TOPPING THE RIDGE...MOVES ENE FROM WY/MT INTO NRN MN/WRN ONT. AT THE SAME TIME...THE JAMES BAY TROUGH WILL AMPLIFY SE TOWARD THE ST LAWRENCE VLY...SUBSTANTIALLY LOWERING HEIGHTS OVER THE NERN U.S. AT THE SFC...COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH THE AB TROUGH WILL ACCELERATE SE INTO THE NRN PLNS LATER TODAY/TNGT...OVERTAKING WEAKER FRONTAL SYSTEM/SFC WAVE NOW OVER THE DAKOTAS. IN THE NORTHEAST...A SERIES OF WEAK FRONTAL SURGES WILL ACCOMPANY AMPLIFYING TROUGH IN THAT REGION.

sections.title: NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY/WRN GRT LKS TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: ONGOING COMPLEX MCS IN ERN ND AND MN...INCLUDING SUPERCELL/SMALL BOW NOW NEAR AXN...SHOULD PERSIST THROUGH LATER THIS MORNING....SUPPORTED BY MODERATE BUT VERY MOIST SWLY LLJ BENEATH EML ON NRN FRINGE OF CNTRL/SRN PLNS RIDGE. WHILE EML CAP IS SUBSTANTIAL...STRENGTH OF LLJ AND CONTINUED EWD DEVELOPMENT OF THE JET MAY SUPPORT FORWARD PROPAGATION OF THE MN STORMS ESE/SE ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF THAT STATE AND POSSIBLY INTO WRN WI AS SFC HEATING WARMS INFLOWING AIR LATER TODAY. ON THE W SIDE OF THE MCS...WAA ATOP MCS COLD POOL LIKELY WILL SUPPORT ADDITIONAL REGENERATIVE ACTIVITY IN ERN ND AND FAR WRN MN. THESE STORMS COULD POSE A RISK FOR SVR HAIL AND LOCALLY DMGG WIND GIVEN DEGREE OF ELEVATED CAPE /AOA 2000 J PER KG/. LATER TODAY...SFC HEATING AND INCREASING FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH MT/WY IMPULSE EXPECTED TO SUPPORT A NEW ROUND OF STRONG TO POSSIBLY INTENSE STORMS OVER CNTRL/ERN ND AND PERHAPS NE SD...PRIMARILY ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARY LEFT BY MORNING MCS...BUT ALSO POSSIBLY ALONG DEVELOPING COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH CANADIAN UPR TROUGH. COMBINATION OF VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AIR WITH STEEP MID LVL LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD SBCAPE AOA 4500 J/KG. COUPLED WITH 35-40 KT DEEP WSWLY SHEAR...SE

sections.title: NORTHEAST/MID ATLANTIC THIS AFTN AND EARLY EVE
sections.text: RESIDUAL EML PLUME BEING DRAWN ESEWD AHEAD OF AMPLIFYING ERN CANADIAN TROUGH...IN CONJUNCTION WITH SFC HEATING...SUFFICIENTLY MOIST LOW LVL ENVIRONMENT...AND 30-40 KT NNWLY DEEP SHEAR WILL SUPPORT WDLY SCTD TO SCTD STORMS POSING A THREAT FOR HAIL AND LOCALLY DMGG WIND. SOME OF THE STORMS BRIEFLY MAY ASSUME SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS. WHILE WEAK LOW LVL CONVERGENCE SHOULD LIMIT STORM COVERAGE...PRESENCE OF SUBSTANTIAL DEEP DIRECTIONAL SHEAR WITH RELATIVELY STEEP LOW TO MID LVL LAPSE RATES SUGGEST THAT SVR POTENTIAL WILL BE SUFFICIENTLY GREAT TO WARRANT EXTENSION OF SLIGHT RISK AREA WWD INTO OH AND SWD INTO MD/DE. THE STORMS MAY EVOLVE INTO SEVERAL SMALL CLUSTERS/BROKEN BANDS AS THEY MOVE/DEVELOP SEWD...WITH A DIMINISHING THREAT FOR ISOLD SVR WIND AND POSSIBLY HAIL CONTINUING INTO THIS EVE OVER THE MID ATLANTIC REGION AND PARTS OF NEW ENGLAND.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST/GULF CST THIS AFTN
sections.text: ALONG/SOUTH OF A SLOW MOVING FRONT/BOUNDARY ACROSS THE REGION...POCKETS OF STRONG HEATING COUPLED WITH HIGH PW WILL YIELD AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR ISOLD TO SCTD STORMS WITH WET MICROBURSTS.

sections.title: WRN STATES THIS AFTN/EARLY EVE
sections.text: BETWEEN THE PLNS RIDGE AND MODEST CYCLONIC SW TO WSW FLOW THE FAR WEST...STRONG SFC HEATING BENEATH BROAD CORRIDOR OF INCREASING MID/UPR LVL MOISTURE WILL SUPPORT SCTD STORMS CAPABLE OF ISOLD DOWNBURSTS AND PERHAPS HAIL THIS AFTN/EARLY EVE. ..CORFIDI/COHEN.. 08/01/2011

sections.title: NRN PLAINS INTO UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: APEX OF MIDLEVEL RIDGE WILL BREAK DOWN DURING THE D1 PERIOD OWING TO EWD PROGRESSION OF STRONG SHORT WAVE TROUGH ACROSS THE CANADIAN PRAIRIE PROVINCES AND LOWER-LATITUDE IMPULSES LIFTING NEWD FROM THE GREAT BASIN/NRN HIGH PLAINS. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE LOW OVER N-CNTRL SD WILL DEVELOP EWD ALONG AGGREGATE OUTFLOW-WARM FRONTAL BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING THROUGH CNTRL MN. MEANWHILE...A COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE SEWD THROUGH THE NRN PLAINS. MCS ONGOING ACROSS MN MAY PERSIST TODAY WITH A CONTINUED RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL PRIMARILY ALONG WRN/UPSHEAR FLANK OF SYSTEM WHERE LOW-LEVEL INFLOW OF A MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR MASS IS MAINTAINED BY SWLY LLJ. ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS ANTICIPATED THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING FARTHER W ACROSS THE DAKOTAS ALONG COLD FRONT AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/WARM FRONT WHERE LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE IS MAXIMIZED. HERE...THE COMBINATION OF VERY STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOW/MID 70S WILL YIELD AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-4500+ J/KG. THIS INSTABILITY WILL COINCIDE WITH WIND PROFILES EXHIBITING PRONOUNCED VEERING WITH HEIGHT AND 40-50 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR. AS SUCH...INITIAL STORM MODE WILL LIKELY BE SUPERCELL

sections.title: NERN U.S. WWD INTO THE UPPER OH VALLEY
sections.text: STRONG UPPER-LEVEL JET STREAK WILL DIG SSEWD THROUGH THE LOWER GREAT LAKES INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES CONTRIBUTING TO THE AMPLIFICATION OF LARGE-SCALE TROUGH PROGRESSING SEWD THROUGH ERN CANADA AND THE NERN CONUS. THIS UPPER-AIR PATTERN EVOLUTION WILL SUPPORT THE SEWD ADVANCEMENT OF SURFACE COLD FRONT THROUGH THE REGION DURING THE D1 PERIOD. DAYTIME HEATING COMBINED WITH A NARROW RIBBON OF EML AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S WILL RESULT IN AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION TODAY AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT WITH MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-3000 J/KG. HEIGHT FALLS/DYNAMIC FORCING FOR ASCENT AND CONVERGENCE ALONG COLD FRONT WILL FOSTER AN INCREASE IN TSTMS ACROSS REGION...SOME OF WHICH COULD BE SEVERE. DESPITE THE SSEWD-PROGRESSION OF UPPER-LEVEL JET STREAK...LOW TO MID-TROPOSPHERIC WIND FIELD IS NOT FORECAST TO BE PARTICULARLY STRONG WITH RESULTANT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR MAGNITUDES OF GENERALLY 30 KT OR LESS. THIS MAY TEND TO LIMIT THE POTENTIAL FOR MORE ORGANIZED STORM MODES AND WIDESPREAD SEVERE WEATHER. NONETHELESS...SETUP WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF MULTICELL OR MARGINAL SUPERCELL CLUSTERS AND/OR LINE SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND HAIL.

sections.title: INTER-MOUNTAIN WEST
sections.text: NEWD PROGRESSION OF SHORT WAVE TROUGH FROM THE GREAT BASIN INTO NRN HIGH PLAINS TODAY WILL MAINTAIN THE TRANSPORT OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE FROM THE GULF OF CA THROUGH AZ...UT/WRN CO INTO WY...SUPPORTING POCKETS OF MODEST AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION. THOUGH VERTICAL SHEAR WILL NOT BE PARTICULARLY STRONG...ISOLATED OCCURRENCES OF DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE OWING TO STEEPENING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DEEPENING SUB-CLOUD LAYERS. ..MEAD/GARNER.. 08/01/2011

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS/UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: CURRENT THINKING IS THAT PRIMARY SCENARIO FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE NIGHT IS FOR THE POTENTIAL OF ADDITIONAL SEVERE TSTM DEVELOPMENT NEAR/NORTH-NORTHEAST OF AN OUTFLOW REINFORCED WARM FRONT THAT ANGLES FROM NEAR THE DAKOTAS BORDER SOUTHEASTWARD INTO SOUTH-CENTRAL MN. AIDED BY GLANCING DPVA/GRADUAL HEIGHT FALLS THE REMAINDER OF THE NIGHT...A NOCTURNALLY INCREASING LOW LEVEL JET/ASSOCIATED WARM ADVECTION SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO SUCH DEVELOPMENT. GIVEN A VERY UNSTABLE SOURCE REGION AIRMASS...REFLECTED BY THE 5500 J/KG MLCAPE AS PER THE 00Z ABERDEEN OBSERVED SOUNDING...LARGE HAIL POTENTIAL WILL EXIST...AND A TORNADO CANNOT BE RULED OUT PROVIDED DEVELOPMENT NEAR THE WARM FRONT. OTHERWISE...STORMS MAY EVENTUALLY GROW UPSCALE AND SPREAD EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS MN TOWARD WI/UPPER MI.

sections.title: NORTHEAST/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: SEVERE HAIL/WIND WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE BUT ON AN INCREASINGLY MARGINAL/ISOLATED BASIS THIS EVENING AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO COOL/DECOUPLE. ..GUYER.. 08/02/2011
